class-object-encapsulation:
## Validate state at the boundary
An invariant is a rule that must remain true while an object is used. For an order total, reject negative values in the constructor and in any method that adds or subtracts money. Use BigDecimal created from a string for monetary values and choose an explicit rounding rule.

Start fields as private. Expose operations such as confirm or addItem instead of unrestricted setters. A getter/setter pair does not protect a rule if the setter accepts any value. A final reference cannot be reassigned, but its target may still be mutable. Protect mutable collections with defensive copies when designing immutable objects.
interface-polymorphism-composition:
## Choose a contract before an implementation
PaymentGateway declares what Checkout needs: a charge operation. BankGateway performs a real charge, while FakeGateway records an amount for a test. A PaymentGateway variable can hold either implementation; dynamic dispatch selects the method using the actual object’s runtime type.

Composition means Checkout has a gateway. Inheritance would mean Checkout is a kind of gateway, which does not describe this relationship. Pass the gateway through the constructor so tests can substitute a fake. Use inheritance only when a subtype fulfills the entire superclass contract. An Override annotation lets the compiler catch a mismatched implementation signature.
collections-generics-records:
## Match the collection to the lookup
List preserves order and permits duplicates. Set stores unique elements. Map connects a unique key to a value, making Map<Long, Order> a natural choice for ID-based lookup. Declare the interface type and select HashMap, LinkedHashMap, or another implementation according to the behavior you need.

Generics reject incompatible types at compile time. Optional makes an absent lookup result explicit; it is most useful as a return type. A record generates its constructor, accessors, equals, hashCode, and toString. Its components are final, but a referenced collection is not automatically immutable. HashMap and ArrayList need additional care when multiple threads write to them.
exception-resource-lifecycle:
## Handle failure and cleanup separately
Checked exceptions must be caught or declared. RuntimeException subclasses are unchecked. Select handling based on what the caller can actually do: recover, translate the failure with additional context, or let a more appropriate layer handle it. Preserve the original exception as the cause when wrapping it.

Use try-with-resources for AutoCloseable resources such as readers and streams. It closes resources when the block exits, including exceptional exits, and closes multiple resources in reverse order. An empty catch block discards the evidence of failure. A domain-specific exception can describe the business outcome and later be mapped to an HTTP response.
single-responsibility:
## Separate reasons to change
SRP does not impose a one-method class or a line limit. Ask which actors or requirements can cause the class to change. Pricing rules, database storage, and email templates usually evolve for different reasons. Keeping them in one class makes a change to one responsibility affect tests and dependencies for the others.

Extract a calculator, repository, and notifier, then coordinate them in a service. Keep related behavior together: splitting every line into another class makes the flow harder to follow. The goal is a boundary that matches change, not a particular class count.
open-closed:
## Add a strategy through an interface
A long conditional over discount types must be edited whenever another type appears. If the same branching exists in several places, a new discount requires coordinated edits. Extract DiscountPolicy and let Checkout call apply without knowing each policy’s class.

Choose the implementation in one composition point. In Spring, a map of policy beans can make selection explicit. Open/Closed does not mean stable code can never change. It means known variation points can be extended without repeatedly editing the central flow. Avoid building interfaces, factories, and plugin loaders for variations that have no concrete requirement.
liskov-interface-segregation:
## Preserve the behavior callers rely on
A subtype must honor the input conditions and results promised by its contract. It should not reject quantities the interface permits or return null where the contract promises a value. A read-only repository that throws from save cannot fulfill a combined read/write contract.

Split that contract into OrderReader and OrderWriter. Reporting code then requests only OrderReader, while an implementation supporting both can implement both interfaces. Smaller interfaces make fakes easier to write. A familiar real-world relationship is not enough to justify inheritance: mutable Square and Rectangle types can violate expectations about independently setting width and height.
dependency-inversion:
## Let business code own the contract
Checkout should describe the payment operation it needs through PaymentGateway. BankGateway implements that interface and adapts the requirement to a vendor API. Changing the vendor should not force the business flow to depend on a new concrete client.

Dependency injection supplies an object from outside. Dependency inversion determines which direction the source-code dependency points. Injecting a concrete BankGateway uses DI without necessarily applying DIP. An ordinary main method can act as the composition root; Spring’s container can fill that role later. Constructor injection makes required dependencies visible and allows fields to be final.
jdk-maven-project:
## Start with a consistent toolchain
Use Java 21 for this learning path. The examples follow Spring Boot 3-style projects; when using another major version, check its system requirements and migration notes. In Spring Initializr choose Java, Maven, and the Web, Validation, and Actuator dependencies.

The starter parent manages compatible dependency versions. Keep the main application class in a parent package so component scanning finds its subpackages. Maven Wrapper records the Maven version for both developer machines and CI. Lifecycle phases run in sequence: validate, compile, test, package, verify, and install. After startup, inspect /actuator/health to check the running application.
ioc-constructor-injection:
## Let Spring connect the object graph
ApplicationContext manages objects called beans. Component, Service, Repository, and RestController are common component-scanned stereotypes. For an object from a library, declare a Bean method inside Configuration instead of editing the library class.

A single constructor can state required dependencies without Autowired. Default singleton beans are shared by concurrent requests, so do not put the current request or order in a service field. Use parameters, local variables, or durable storage. When several beans implement one interface, choose with Primary or Qualifier, or request a collection of all candidates. Constructor cycles usually indicate responsibilities that need separating.
controller-service-repository:
## Keep transport details at the edge
RestController serializes return values into the HTTP response body. GetMapping selects a route, PathVariable reads a path segment, and RequestParam reads a query parameter. The controller delegates use-case behavior to a service, which can be tested without HTTP.

Repositories handle data access. Business rules belong in service/domain code so a message consumer or scheduled task can reuse them. Three layers are a starting point rather than a required class count. For richer domains, methods such as order.confirm() can hold invariants while a service coordinates the operation. Organize packages by feature when that keeps code that changes together close together.
configuration-profiles:
## Run one artifact with different configuration
Keep database URLs, timeouts, and credentials separate from the built JAR. In a simplified precedence order, command-line arguments override environment variables, which override packaged configuration. Relaxed binding uses uppercase environment names, replaces dots with underscores, and removes hyphens.

Bind related properties into a ConfigurationProperties record instead of scattering Value expressions. Register it with ConfigurationPropertiesScan or EnableConfigurationProperties. Profiles group environment-specific behavior; environment variables are often simpler for values. Never commit passwords, tokens, or API keys. Supply them through a secret manager or platform mechanism, and rotate a secret that was accidentally committed.
resource-http-status:
## Describe operations with HTTP semantics
Use plural resource URLs such as /orders and /orders/42. GET reads, POST creates or initiates work, PUT replaces, PATCH partially updates, and DELETE removes. Safe methods do not request a state change; idempotent methods have the same intended effect when repeated.

Use 201 with Location for creation, 200 for a response body, and 204 for successful operations without one. Invalid input commonly returns 400; missing authentication returns 401; insufficient permission returns 403; a missing resource returns 404. Do not hide failures in a 200 response containing an error field. Clients, monitoring, and retry logic rely on HTTP status.
dto-bean-validation:
## Separate the public payload from persistence
An entity follows the domain and database mapping. A DTO follows the public API contract. Returning entities directly can expose fields, couple the API to schema changes, and trigger lazy queries during serialization. Records are a concise option for request and response DTOs.

Declare constraints such as NotBlank, Min, Positive, Size, and Email on input fields. Add Valid to the controller’s RequestBody argument so Spring checks them before calling the service. Constraints validate the input itself; checking stock or order state still belongs in business logic. Frontend validation improves usability but cannot replace server validation.
error-response-problemdetail:
## Give clients a predictable error format
Problem Details defines type, title, status, detail, and instance. Spring’s ProblemDetail supports that format and can include additional properties, such as validation field errors. RestControllerAdvice centralizes mappings from domain exceptions to HTTP responses.

Use a specific handler for a missing order and map it to 404. ResponseEntityExceptionHandler can customize framework validation responses. Keep stack traces, SQL messages, table names, file paths, and uncontrolled exception details out of public errors. For unexpected failures, return a generic message with a correlation ID and record the detailed diagnostics in server logs using that ID.
api-contract-edge-cases:
## Document each outcome, not just successful examples
An API contract includes method, path, payload constraints, status, response shape, and headers such as Location or Idempotency-Key. List cases for missing required fields, out-of-range values, malformed JSON, wrong content type, missing credentials, and missing resources.

Keep repeatable curl commands with expected responses in the project and promote them to automated HTTP tests. Renaming or removing fields, changing a type, making optional input required, or changing status semantics can break clients. Additive changes are often easier to migrate. OpenAPI helps describe a larger API, but generated specifications still need meaningful examples and documented failures.
entity-repository:
## Map objects and control the persistence boundary
JPA specifies object-relational mapping, Hibernate implements it, and Spring Data supplies repository behavior. Entity identifies the mapped class; Id marks its key; GeneratedValue chooses key generation. Use a protected no-argument constructor for JPA and store enums as strings when order changes must not reinterpret old data.

JpaRepository supplies common operations, paging, and sorting. Derived query method names select properties and operators; Query handles explicit JPQL. Disable open-in-view when you want loading requirements to be resolved in the service rather than during JSON serialization. Enable SQL logging during development so hidden database work is visible.
local-transactions:
## Commit related changes together
Creating an order may save the order, items, and audit data. Put the local unit of work in a transactional service method so a failure can roll back related changes. Default Spring rollback rules apply to RuntimeException and Error; configure rollbackFor if checked exceptions should also roll back.

Hibernate tracks managed entities in a persistence context and flushes changes at commit. Spring transaction annotations normally work through proxies, so calls through this do not start a new proxy-managed transaction. Avoid slow HTTP or email work while holding database locks. A local transaction cannot undo an HTTP operation or broker publish in another system.
schema-migration:
## Version database changes alongside code
Flyway reads ordered migrations from src/main/resources/db/migration and records versions and checksums in flyway_schema_history. Name a migration V2__add_order_status.sql, including two underscores. Do not edit a script that has already been applied elsewhere; create a new version.

Let migrations change the schema and use Hibernate validate or none. For a required column on existing rows, add a compatible nullable column, backfill data, release code that fills it, and tighten the constraint later. This expand-and-contract approach supports old and new application versions during rollout. Rolling back an application does not reverse a database migration.
relations-query-cost:
## Inspect what relationship access actually loads
OneToMany and ManyToOne describe relationships. mappedBy marks the inverse side; cascade and orphanRemoval affect related persistence operations. Choose fetching according to the use case rather than making every relation eager.

Loading twenty orders and then lazily loading each item collection can produce twenty-one queries: the N+1 problem. Inspect SQL or Hibernate statistics, not only local response time. JOIN FETCH and EntityGraph can load required associations explicitly. A DTO projection can read only the columns needed. Collection fetch joins and pagination need care: fetching page IDs and then the relationships avoids loading a full collection result just to page it in memory.
unit-test-bisnis:
## Test behavior without starting the framework
Arrange creates inputs and dependencies, Act performs one operation, and Assert checks the observable result. Name tests after behavior so a failure explains what stopped working. Constructor injection lets a unit test use ordinary new expressions instead of SpringBootTest.

A fake is a working simplified implementation, a stub provides predetermined answers, and a mock records interactions for verification. Avoid asserting every internal call when a meaningful result is available. Inject Clock or a generator to control time and randomness. Keep unit tests independent of network access and execution order so repeated runs are reliable.
integration-testcontainers:
## Exercise the actual database behavior
Unit tests cannot establish that mappings, JPQL, SQL migrations, and database constraints work together. H2 may differ from PostgreSQL in types, functions, and errors. A PostgreSQL Testcontainer lets integration tests use the technology used by the application.

Container manages lifecycle; a static field shares a container across the test class. ServiceConnection supplies connection details. DataJpaTest loads the persistence slice, and Replace.NONE prevents substitution with an embedded database. Container startup has a cost, so reuse an appropriate lifecycle rather than starting one for each method. Podman users need a compatible Docker API socket; macOS and Windows also need the Linux VM running.
auth-jwt-resource-server:
## Verify identity before checking permission
Authentication establishes who called; authorization decides which action is allowed. A resource server verifies tokens from an authorization server instead of implementing login itself. A JWT payload is encoded rather than encrypted, and decoding it does not verify its signature.

Configure the issuer, expected audience when applicable, and a JWT resource server. Map scopes to authorities such as SCOPE_orders:write. Put specific request rules before anyRequest. Missing or invalid credentials return 401; a valid caller without the required scope gets 403. Resource-level ownership checks still belong in the service: a read scope does not grant access to every user’s order.
test-jalur-gagal:
## Test the contract at the HTTP boundary
Validation and authorization can regress while the happy path keeps working. Use a web slice to check responses for missing tokens, insufficient scopes, invalid bodies, and missing IDs. Mock service behavior so each test focuses on its HTTP outcome.

MockMvc JWT request post-processors can supply an authenticated test identity without a running authorization server; that does not test cryptographic verification itself. Keep separate tests for the required security behavior. Line coverage shows which lines executed, not whether a meaningful assertion was made. Run the suite in CI on each pull request to detect changed access rules and error mappings.
monolith-atau-microservices:
## Choose boundaries before distribution
Microservices organize independently running services around business capabilities. Independent releases and scaling can help, but HTTP failures, distributed data, tracing, and operations all add work. A modular monolith can preserve module boundaries within a single deployment.

Separate a service for a concrete need, such as a different release rhythm, scaling pattern, or isolation requirement. Splitting by table or technical layer can create services that must still change together. Record the decision and consequences in an ADR. The examples use Order, Inventory, and Notification so the communication problems remain understandable without a large system.
batas-domain-ownership:
## Assign one owner to each data set
Order owns order state, Inventory owns stock and reservations, and Notification owns delivery records. Other services use the owner’s API for immediate data or consume events to build the local view they need. Direct cross-service SQL makes an internal schema a hidden public contract.

A bounded context defines where a model and its language are meaningful; the same word need not have the same representation in every service. Watch changes over time: if every feature modifies and releases two services together, reconsider the boundary. A long chain of synchronous calls is another sign that the design needs review.
komunikasi-sinkron:
## Budget time and map downstream errors
A network call can fail to connect, lose a response, or wait on a slow dependency. Configure connection and read timeouts that fit the overall user operation. Use Boot’s instrumented RestClient.Builder rather than manually discarding its configuration.

Map an Inventory stock conflict to a domain conflict; map an unavailable Inventory dependency to a useful service-unavailable response. An invalid request sent by Order may instead indicate an Order bug. Keep callers from receiving raw technical exceptions. Required synchronous dependency availability compounds, so shorten chains or use events for operations such as notification that do not require an immediate result.
deployment-data-independen:
## Release providers without breaking running consumers
Independent deployment requires compatible contracts, separate release processes, and controlled data access. During a rolling update, old and new versions may run together. Add a new field first, migrate consumers, confirm the old field is unused, and only then remove it.

Consumer-driven contract tests express what a consumer expects and verify providers before release. Database-per-service does not always require a separate server: separate schemas and users can enforce a boundary on one PostgreSQL instance. Do not rely only on naming conventions. Use events, an explicit read model, or a warehouse for cross-service reporting rather than reaching into private schemas.
timeout-retry-idempotency:
## Retry only within a safe policy
A 503 or transport timeout may be transient. A malformed request or a business conflict usually needs a changed request instead. Bound attempts and the overall deadline, increase delay with exponential backoff, and add jitter to avoid many clients retrying together.

After a POST timeout, the caller cannot know whether the server committed. Send one idempotency key for the logical operation and reuse it for retries. Persist the key, payload fingerprint, and result atomically with the business change. Reject reuse for a different payload. An in-memory map does not coordinate replicas or survive restart, so production storage and a retention policy are required.
circuit-breaker:
## Stop repeated calls to an unhealthy dependency
CLOSED forwards and records calls. When enough samples show a failure rate above the threshold, OPEN rejects new calls immediately. After a wait, HALF_OPEN allows limited probes. Successful probes close the circuit; failed probes reopen it.

A fallback should represent a valid alternative, such as acceptable cached data or a clear unavailable response. Do not invent available stock or a successful payment. Circuit breakers complement timeouts, bounded retries, bulkheads, and rate limits. When combining retry with a breaker, avoid retrying CallNotPermittedException while the circuit is open. The playground is a simplified sequential model with virtual time.
event-ack-duplikasi:
## Acknowledge completed work and expect redelivery
Publisher confirm reports broker acceptance; consumer acknowledgement reports completed consumption. They protect different links. Acknowledging before processing can lose work if the consumer crashes. Acknowledging afterward allows redelivery if it crashes after processing but before acknowledging.

Identify each event with a stable publisher-assigned ID and record processed IDs with a unique constraint. Database deduplication alone cannot atomically cover an external email send; pass an idempotency key to the provider when supported. Limit retries for poison messages and route failures to a dead-letter queue for investigation. Consumers need to tolerate duplicates even when an outbox is used.
outbox-saga:
## Make the durable intent part of the local commit
Writing a database row and publishing to a broker are two separate operations. Either can succeed while the other fails. Store the business change and outbox event in the same local transaction. A relay publishes stored events later and records delivery progress. It may resend after a crash, so consumers remain idempotent.

A saga coordinates a business operation across local transactions. When payment fails after stock reservation, release the reservation and cancel the order. Compensation is a new business action, not a distributed rollback. Choreography reacts to events; orchestration centralizes commands. Expose intermediate states clearly while eventual consistency is being resolved.
health-endpoint:
## Expose enough operational information without leaking internals
Actuator health reports application components; info can report build identity; metrics and prometheus expose measurements. Configuration and heap endpoints can contain secrets or personal information. Use explicit exposure lists and appropriate access controls.

Health indicators contribute to an aggregate result. A database failure can produce DOWN and HTTP 503; UP normally returns 200. A custom indicator should represent a useful check without making every dependency failure a reason to restart. Detailed health and build identity help incident investigation, but do not expose sensitive configuration simply because an endpoint is operational.
logs-metrics-traces:
## Use each signal for the question it answers
Metrics answer how often, how long, and how much. Logs explain events with context. Traces identify the path and duration of operations within a request. A common investigation starts with an error-rate alert, follows a trace to the failing service, then reads related logs.

Micrometer provides Counter, Gauge, Timer, and DistributionSummary. Keep tag cardinality bounded: order IDs and emails create too many series. Use parameterized logging, choose levels deliberately, and include trace identifiers when available. Do not log passwords, bearer tokens, full headers, or customer identity data. Send metrics to an appropriate backend such as Prometheus.
tracing-antarservice:
## Propagate context across instrumented boundaries
A trace contains spans for operations such as an HTTP request or database call. Each span has timing, status, and attributes. The W3C traceparent header carries the IDs needed for the next service to join the same trace.

Spring Boot integrates Micrometer Tracing with supported bridges and exporters. Use the configured client builder so observation instrumentation adds context headers. A manually created RestClient may start an unrelated trace downstream. Confirm exporter properties against your framework version. Sampling limits production storage and processing; development may use 100%, while collector-side tail sampling can retain failures and slow requests selectively.
liveness-readiness-startup:
## Make probe failures trigger the right action
Readiness controls whether a pod receives traffic. Liveness triggers a container restart when the process cannot make progress. Startup probes allow initialization to finish before liveness and readiness checks take effect. A slow JVM startup should not be mistaken for an unrecoverable process.

Use separate Actuator health groups. Do not include a shared database in liveness: its outage would restart every instance without fixing the dependency. Readiness checks for shared dependencies also need thought; removing every endpoint can be less informative than a clear application error. Configure realistic initial timing, periods, and thresholds for the application’s startup and recovery behavior.
image-container-registry:
## Package once and distribute the artifact
An image contains filesystem layers and configuration such as environment defaults and the entrypoint. A container starts from an image and adds a writable layer. Linux namespaces isolate what it can see; cgroups constrain resources. It shares a kernel rather than carrying a full virtual-machine kernel.

A registry distributes images between build and runtime machines. Use explicit registry names and release tags, then record a digest when content identity matters. latest is only a tag and can point to different content over time. Container-local files disappear when the container is removed unless data is stored in a volume. Docker and Podman use OCI image standards.
dockerfile-non-root:
## Separate build tools from the runtime
A basic Dockerfile can copy a prebuilt JAR, but a multi-stage build also controls the JDK and Maven used for compilation. Copy dependency descriptors before frequently changed source files to improve cache reuse. Exclude Git data, local build products, and editor files from the build context.

Run the JVM as a non-root numeric user and grant only the directory permissions it needs. Use the JSON exec form of ENTRYPOINT so stop signals reach the process. EXPOSE is documentation; publish ports explicitly with -p. A loopback host binding avoids exposing a local practice application to the whole network.
network-volume-compose:
## Use networks for access and volumes for durability
A container normally has its own localhost. Put the app and database on a shared user-defined network and use the database service name as its hostname. Store PostgreSQL data in a named volume; use a bind mount for a deliberately shared host file when appropriate.

Compose declares the service graph, network, environment, and volumes. A simple depends_on waits for startup order, while service_healthy waits for a successful healthcheck. The application still must handle later connection loss. Keep shared-project secrets outside committed files and use platform secret facilities when deploying beyond a local exercise.
podman-rootless:
## Diagnose the process before changing privileges
Podman can run rootless and without a central root daemon. Linux containers on macOS and Windows need Podman’s Linux VM. Initialize it once and start it before running containers. Use fully qualified image names to avoid ambiguous short-name resolution.

For a failing container, inspect process state, startup logs, port mappings, and the listen address. Check UID mapping and SELinux labels for volume permissions rather than using privileged mode as a shortcut. Root inside a user namespace is not host root. Containers in one pod can share a network namespace, unlike unrelated containers on an ordinary network.
ocp-kubernetes-project:
## Describe desired state to the cluster
Kubernetes schedules workloads and reconciles desired state. OpenShift adds developer tools, Routes, an integrated registry, and security controls around that platform. Developers usually interact through the API using manifests and the oc CLI rather than managing individual host processes.

A project scopes resource names, access, and quotas. Select the intended project before applying a manifest. Use get to inspect state, describe for details and events, logs for application output, and apply for declarative changes. This introduction covers deploying and exposing an application; cluster installation, node operations, and platform administration require separate study.
pod-deployment-service:
## Keep stable addressing separate from replaceable pods
A Pod groups containers that share networking and selected volumes. Pods are temporary: replacement can change their names and IPs. Deployment manages ReplicaSets to maintain the requested replicas and coordinate rollout. Its selector must match the pod template labels.

Service provides a stable address and selects matching ready pods. Use its DNS name rather than hard-coding a pod IP. ConfigMap carries ordinary configuration; Secret supplies credentials. The same image can run with different environment settings. Readiness and rollout settings influence continuity, and application rollback still does not undo an already applied database migration.
route-akses:
## Connect an external hostname to a Service
An OpenShift Route maps an external hostname through the router to a Service. With edge termination, TLS ends at the router and the internal hop uses HTTP. Passthrough leaves TLS for the pod, while re-encrypt establishes another TLS connection from router to pod.

Redirect plain HTTP to HTTPS when appropriate. Applications behind a trusted proxy need correct forwarded-header handling when building public URLs; configure that together with the deployment’s trust boundary. For a 503, check readiness, Service selectors, target ports, and pod endpoints before changing the application. A running pod is not necessarily ready to receive traffic.
arbitrary-uid-resources:
## Make the image work with the assigned identity
OpenShift’s restricted execution model assigns a UID from the project range. Required writable directories should use appropriate group ownership and group permissions rather than assuming one fixed UID or asking for broad SCC privileges. Test locally with a different UID and the expected group.

Declare CPU and memory requests for scheduling and limits for runtime control. Memory above the limit may result in OOMKilled. JVM memory includes metaspace, stacks, buffers, and code cache as well as heap, so do not assign the entire container limit to heap. Measure usage and tune both application settings and resource limits.
rancang-dokumentasi:
## Keep the capstone small enough to verify
Build Order, Inventory, and Notification around one complete order flow. A customer submits products and quantities, stock is reserved, the order is confirmed, and a notification is sent. Document stock exhaustion, dependency timeout, duplicate requests, and failed notification delivery as well.

Assign ownership of order state, stock, idempotency records, and delivery logs. Write API payloads, statuses, headers, and event schemas before implementation. Record at least the service boundary, event choice, and consistency strategy in ADRs. Define completion in terms of working behavior, repeatable tests, runnable images, useful signals, and a README another person can follow.
bangun-uji-kegagalan:
## Add one verifiable stage at a time
Start with Order and its validation, persistence, migrations, and tests. Add Inventory’s reservation API, connect it with bounded HTTP calls, then add idempotency, a breaker, an outbox, and an idempotent Notification consumer. Add health, metrics, and tracing so failures can be investigated.

Maintain a failure matrix with a trigger, expected result, and evidence. Include a stopped or slow Inventory service, repeated POSTs, conflicting key reuse, duplicate events, failed transactions, and broker downtime. Use automated tests where practical and reproducible manual steps elsewhere. Playground simulations explain concepts but do not replace evidence from the actual capstone.
build-release-deploy:
## Promote the same tested artifact
A release pipeline runs unit and integration tests, builds and tags an image, pushes it, deploys to staging, and verifies health and smoke tests before production. Keep the image identical across environments and supply URLs, credentials, and runtime settings externally.

Write rollout, verification, and rollback commands before an incident. Record the previous image digest. Schema compatibility matters: a previous application version cannot run if a migration removed a column it still needs. Demonstrate the image locally with Compose and optionally in an OpenShift sandbox. Compare digests to confirm that deployment did not rebuild the application into a different artifact.
review-serah-terima:
## Have someone follow the operational instructions
A handover README should cover prerequisites, local startup, test commands, environment settings, deployment, health checks, troubleshooting, and recovery. Try it on a clean machine or VM and record every assumption the reader cannot infer.

State known limitations with their impact and planned handling. Examples include an outbox relay restricted to one replica or compensation requiring a manual step. Review service boundaries, authorization, timeouts, safe retries, deduplication, migrations, image permissions, observability, and secret handling. The goal is a project another person can operate and verify from the documentation, including its unsupported conditions.
